Summary:
The appendix of the back-door detection paper presents a complete reasoning chain from the security risk of hidden back-doors in neural-network classifiers, through the empirical regularities that allow detectors to spot them, to two concrete mitigation strategies: (1) anomaly-index–based screening that reverse-engineers minimal triggers with only limited test data, and (2) neuron pruning guided by the reverse trigger to deactivate the back-door while preserving clean accuracy. Extensive experiments on six image-classification datasets validate both techniques.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]  
The instructions were followed closely; all reasoning steps contained in the text were mapped to concept nodes, white-box decomposition was applied, and every node is connected to the fabric. Remaining uncertainty comes from having only the appendix rather than the full paper, so a few causal labels relied on moderate inference.

Inference strategy justification:
Where the appendix only implied causal links (e.g. that small-norm triggers arise from attacker-poisoned labels), moderate inference (confidence 2) was used, clearly marked in edge rationales.

Extraction completeness explanation:
The appendix repeatedly revisits exactly two intervention ideas (detection via anomaly index; mitigation via pruning). All intermediate assumptions, design choices, implementation details and validation figures mentioned were captured, giving eleven concept nodes and two intervention nodes (≈13 nodes for ≈3 k words).

Key limitations:
• The full methodology section was missing, so some details (e.g. exact optimisation hyper-parameters) could not be captured.  
• Only image-classification back-doors were studied; generalisation to other modalities was not discussed and thus not included.
